skill.description: Review fiction, screenplays, and outlines through evidence-based diagnosis, competing explanations, targeted revisions, and checks for unintended changes.
skill.summary: Test story diagnoses before revising, track coverage of long works, and prepare producer review plans.

content.value_statement: AI story feedback can repeat an unsupported diagnosis and encourage unnecessary changes. This skill tests competing explanations against textual evidence before recommending focused revisions.
actual_capabilities: Generate competing story diagnoses and test them with counterexamples and counterfactual questions.
Anchor major claims to textual observations while separating evidence, inference, and diagnosis.
Recommend minimal interventions and check their effects on voice, ambiguity, pacing, and other protected qualities.
Track source coverage across chapters, episodes, files, and versions before making work-wide claims.
Compile season-outline reviews into decision pages, issue routes, hard-error lists, and dependency-ordered revision task cards.
Record changes in each diagnosis and stop when another review loop adds no meaningful information.
limitations: Results depend on the underlying model and the completeness of the story material supplied.
The documented benchmarks are development evidence, not independent proof of superiority over a strong prompt.
The skill does not replace human editorial approval, legal review, rights clearance, or production decisions.
The workflow supports diagnosis and permitted targeted revision, not a dedicated full-manuscript rewrite process.

use_cases.title: Review a novel draft
use_cases.description: Compare explanations for weak character agency across chapters while preserving voice and ambiguity.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a screenplay scene
use_cases.description: Check objectives, choices, and state changes before selecting the smallest useful scene revision.

use_cases.title: Prepare a season revision handoff
use_cases.description: Trace major outline problems to their first appearance and organize supported fixes into prioritized revision tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Diagnose one scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the scene below with Socratic Story Cartographer for one loop. Do not rewrite. Give textual evidence and the smallest useful next step. Scene: [text].
prompt_templates.scenario: First review of a short scene

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Test competing diagnoses
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chapter for up to three loops. Compare two plausible causes of the main problem. Test both against textual evidence. Preserve ambiguity and voice. Do not rewrite yet. Chapter: [text].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Verify a multi-file character arc
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these canonical chapter files using the long-work evidence protocol: [files]. Treat [older version] as non-canonical context. Track coverage and test whether the protagonist lacks agency. Inspect later choices before making work-wide claims. Disclose unread material and propose only supported changes.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Compile a producer review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this season outline for up to three loops: [outline]. Apply long-work coverage before producer-outline review. Protect [scenes] and preserve [locked ending]. Do not rewrite or imply approval. Deliver a decision page, issue routes, hard errors, and dependency-ordered revision task cards. Include acceptance questions, stop lines, and the next human approval gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Production-oriented outline review with explicit boundaries

output_examples.input: Illustrative scene: A witness hides a letter, explains its contents to herself, then gives it to the detective without hesitation.
output: Current belief: The handover lacks a consequential choice rather than an explanation of motive.
Evidence anchors: She initially hides the letter, but later gives it away without resistance or a new event.
Competing diagnosis: The explanatory passage may remove uncertainty before the handover.
Counterfactual test: Removing the explanation leaves the same unmotivated handover, so exposition alone does not explain the problem.
Minimal intervention: Establish one immediate cost that makes her decision to hand over the letter meaningful.
Protected quality: Keep her motives partly ambiguous rather than adding a complete explanation.

output_examples.input: Illustrative outline: Episode 2 contains an unsupported agreement that causes an episode 6 betrayal. Episode 5 and the ending are locked.
output: Decision page: Recommend a structural revision proposal for human review, not production approval.
Issue route: The unsupported agreement begins in episode 2; its visible consequence is the betrayal in episode 6.
Revision range: Inspect episodes 2 through 6 instead of patching only the betrayal.
Task objective: Make the agreement depend on an observable pressure or choice.
Acceptance question: Does the revised agreement make the later betrayal causally understandable?
Stop line: Preserve episode 5 and the locked ending; do not introduce a new subplot.
Coverage limit: This brief supports a provisional route, not a complete season assessment.

best_practices: Provide the relevant canonical material, identify older versions, and state which files belong in the review.
Specify your goal, revision permission, protected qualities, and any locked scenes or endings.
Ask for competing explanations and evidence before accepting changes; allow early stopping when further loops add no information.
anti_patterns: Requesting a work-wide diagnosis from isolated excerpts without acknowledging unread material.
Treating author intent, model confidence, or benchmark scores as proof that a diagnosis is correct.
Requiring repeated rewrites despite weak evidence or treating an AI recommendation as human approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is documented for compatible Agent Skills environments, including Claude Code and Codex. Installation and file access depend on the host environment.

faq.question: Must every review run three loops?
faq.answer: No. Three loops is the default maximum. The skill should stop earlier when another loop adds no evidence or useful diagnostic change.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my story automatically?
faq.answer: Revision requires your permission. You can request diagnosis only or allow limited edits while protecting specific story elements.

faq.question: Can it review long manuscripts or multiple files?
faq.answer: It includes a source manifest and coverage ledger protocol. Conclusions must remain limited when files are inaccessible or reading coverage is incomplete.

faq.question: Does it guarantee publication or production readiness?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes text quality from target fit and uncertain acceptance. Human editorial, legal, and production decisions remain separate.

faq.question: Does story review require external services?
faq.answer: No separate story-review service is specified. The documented installation command uses npm and GitHub; your AI host controls model access and data handling.
